correctness.rationale: For valuations (81 all)x3, (100,100,94,94)x5, (94,94,100,100)x5, and (101 all)xp, each agent has total deficit 100 from baseline 101 per item, forcing any PMMS allocation’s bundle sizes to differ by <=1: a pair with difference >=2 can be repartitioned into bundles each worth strictly more than the smaller original bundle. For equal cardinalities k, two-bundle maximin reduces exactly to minimizing maximum deficit across all rare-item triples t; for k and k+1 the short agent compares its deficit to the minimum attainable deficit of the k-side, while long agents automatically pass. Every labeled assignment of the 3 A, 5 B and 5 C rare goods is determined by count compositions; there are C(6,3) C(8,3)^2=62720 profiles. Independent exhaustive exact-integer enumeration over all 62720 profiles at each k=4..13 returned feasible equal-size counts 28,24,8,0,0,0,0,0,0,0. For k>=13 every rare subset fits and comparisons stabilize, proving no equal-size PMMS beyond k=13. The inspected verifier also specifies 15 small-p witnesses and templates for all n=4k+r, r=1,2,3; explicit deficit feasibility and monotonic split-set argument extend each template for all k>=7. Finite enumeration is exhaustive for the bounded certificate only; the infinite periodic statement uses cardinality and k>=13 stabilization. Thus PMMS iff p<15 or (13+p)%4 !=0; first failure p=15, 28 goods, then p=19,23,..., within this particular positive-valued family.
